title: Adding Information
description: Write richer descriptions using non-defining relative clauses, relative clauses with prepositions, reduced relative clauses, and comment clauses with which. Vocabulary: culture, heritage and famous people.
objectives: Use non-defining relative clauses with correct punctuation
Use prepositions in formal and informal relative clauses
Reduce relative clauses with -ing, -ed and to-infinitive forms
Describe people, places and traditions in rich detail

lessons.title: Non-Defining Relative Clauses
lessons.summary: Menambahkan informasi tambahan dengan non-defining relative clause dan tanda koma.
objectives: Distinguish defining and non-defining relative clauses
Use who, which, whose, where and when with commas
Avoid that and omitted pronouns in non-defining clauses
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Two kinds of relative clause
| Defining | Non-defining |
| --- | --- |
| tells us **which one** we mean | adds **extra** information |
| no commas | **commas** (or brackets/dashes) |
| *The woman **who runs the café** is my aunt.* | *My aunt, **who runs a café**, is 60.* |
| removing it changes the meaning | removing it leaves a complete, clear sentence |

### Pronouns in non-defining clauses
| Pronoun | Used for | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| who | people | *Mr. Tan, **who** taught me art, is retiring.* |
| which | things, animals | *The palace, **which** was built in 1820, is open daily.* |
| whose | possession | *Ana, **whose** father is a potter, sells ceramics.* |
| where | places | *Sukamaju, **where** I grew up, is famous for weaving.* |
| when | times | *In 1998, **when** the museum opened, entry was free.* |
| whom | people (object, formal) | *Dr. Lee, **whom** I met in Paris, is a historian.* |

### Three strict rules
1. **No *that***: ✗ *The festival, that takes place in August, ...* → ✓ *which*
2. **Never omit the pronoun**: ✗ *My brother, I live with, ...* → ✓ *My brother, who I live with, ...*
3. **Use commas on both sides** if the clause is in the middle of the sentence.

### Meaning changes with commas
- *My sister **who lives in Bali** is an architect.* → I have more than one sister; I mean the one in Bali.
- *My sister, **who lives in Bali**, is an architect.* → I have one sister; she happens to live in Bali.

### When do we use them?
Non-defining clauses are more common in **writing** than in speech. In conversation, people often use two short sentences or *and*: *My aunt runs a café. She's 60.*

> **Catatan:** Dalam bahasa Indonesia kata *yang* dipakai untuk keduanya, dan tanda koma tidak terlalu mengubah makna. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **koma itu penting**: koma = informasi tambahan, dan setelah koma **tidak boleh** memakai *that*. Nama orang atau tempat yang unik (Mr. Tan, Sukamaju) hampir selalu memakai non-defining clause.

sections.summary: Non-defining relative clauses add **extra information** and need **commas**. Use *who, which, whose, where, when* (and formal *whom*), but **never *that***, and never omit the pronoun. Commas can change the meaning. *Ringkasan: koma = informasi tambahan; tanpa koma = informasi penentu.*

lessons.title: Relative Clauses with Prepositions
lessons.summary: Menggunakan preposisi dalam relative clause: gaya formal (in which, to whom) dan informal (that I live in).
objectives: Place prepositions before whom/which in formal style
Put prepositions at the end of the clause in informal style
Avoid errors such as in where and to who
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Where does the preposition go?
Many verbs and adjectives need a preposition (*talk about, live in, rely on, proud of*). In a relative clause, the preposition can go in two places.

| Style | Pattern | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Formal | preposition + **whom / which** | *The colleague **about whom** I told you is here.* |
| Informal | **who / that / ∅** ... + preposition at the end | *The colleague **(who/that) I told you about** is here.* |

### Formal: preposition + whom/which
- After a preposition, use only **whom** (people) or **which** (things).
- ✗ *to who*, ✗ *about that*
- *The hotel **at which** we stayed was beautiful.*
- *The artist **to whom** the prize was given thanked her family.*

### Informal: preposition at the end
- *The hotel **(that) we stayed at** was beautiful.*
- *That's the museum **I was telling you about**.*
- In defining clauses, the pronoun is often omitted.

### where / when instead of preposition + which
| With preposition | Simpler alternative |
| --- | --- |
| the town **in which** I grew up | the town **where** I grew up |
| the year **in which** we met | the year **when** we met |

⚠️ Don't combine them: ✗ *the town **in where** I grew up*.

### Phrasal verbs
Prepositions that belong to **phrasal verbs** usually stay with the verb, even in formal style: *the problem **which** we **came across*** (NOT *across which we came*).

### Non-defining clauses with prepositions
The same patterns work with commas: *Dr. Lee, **with whom** I studied in Leiden, is now a professor.*

> **Catatan:** Bahasa Indonesia biasanya cukup memakai *yang* atau *tempat*: *hotel tempat kami menginap*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, jangan lupa preposisinya: *the hotel we stayed **at*** atau *the hotel **at which** we stayed*. Setelah preposisi, hanya **whom** dan **which**.

sections.summary: Put the preposition **before whom/which** in formal English (*the town in which*), or **at the end** in informal English (*the town I grew up in*). lessons.title: Reduced Relative Clauses
lessons.summary: Memendekkan relative clause dengan bentuk -ing, -ed (V3), dan to-infinitive.
objectives: Replace active relative clauses with -ing participles
Replace passive relative clauses with past participles
Use the to-infinitive after the first, the last, the only, etc.
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Why reduce?
Reduced relative clauses make writing **shorter and more fluent**. They are very common in news, academic texts and guidebooks.

### 1. Active meaning → -ing participle
Remove the pronoun and use **-ing**:
| Full clause | Reduced |
| --- | --- |
| The woman **who is standing** next to the statue is our guide. | The woman **standing** next to the statue... |
| Visitors **who want** to take photos must pay. | Visitors **wanting** to take photos... |
| a road **that leads** to the temple | a road **leading** to the temple |

The -ing form can replace present or past, simple or continuous verbs: *people **who lived** here 100 years ago* → *people **living** here 100 years ago*.

### 2. Passive meaning → past participle
Remove the pronoun and *be*:
| Full clause | Reduced |
| --- | --- |
| The paintings **which were stolen** in 1990 have been found. | The paintings **stolen** in 1990... |
| a temple **that was built** in the 9th century | a temple **built** in the 9th century |
| the languages **which are spoken** in the region | the languages **spoken** in the region |

### 3. After the first / last / only / next / superlatives → to-infinitive
- *She was **the first woman who climbed** the mountain.* → *She was **the first woman to climb** the mountain.*
- *He's **the only person to have won** the prize twice.*

### When you CAN'T reduce
- When the relative pronoun is the **object**: *the book **that I bought*** (not *the book buying*). Here you can only omit the pronoun: *the book I bought*.
- When the clause describes a **single completed action** in active voice: *The man **who called** yesterday* (not *the man calling yesterday*, which suggests a continuing action).

### Non-defining reduced clauses
They also work with commas: *The palace, **built in 1820**, is now a museum.*

> **Catatan:** Bentuk ini mirip dengan bahasa Indonesia yang menghilangkan *yang*: *orang **berdiri** di sana* (aktif → -ing) dan *lukisan **dicuri** tahun 1990* (pasif → V3). Pikirkan: apakah kata benda itu **melakukan** (-ing) atau **dikenai** (V3) tindakan?

sections.summary: Shorten relative clauses: **active → -ing** (*people living here*), **passive → past participle** (*a temple built in 900*), and **the first/last/only → to-infinitive** (*the first woman to climb*). Don't reduce when the pronoun is the object. *Ringkasan: melakukan → -ing; dikenai → V3.*

lessons.title: Vocabulary: Culture, Heritage and Famous People
lessons.summary: Kosakata tentang budaya, warisan budaya, dan tokoh terkenal.
objectives: Use vocabulary for heritage, traditions and artefacts
Use verbs such as preserve, restore and pass down accurately
Describe famous people with adjectives such as renowned and influential
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Heritage and traditions
| Word | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| heritage | traditions, buildings and culture from the past that a society values | Batik is part of our cultural **heritage**. |
| tradition | a custom passed from generation to generation | It's a **tradition** to visit relatives after Eid. |
| artefact | an object made by people long ago | The museum has 3,000 **artefacts**. |
| monument | a building or statue that honours a person or event | a national **monument** |
| indigenous | originally from a place | **indigenous** languages |
| ancestor | a family member from long ago | Our **ancestors** were farmers. |

### Verbs for protecting the past
| Verb | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| preserve | keep in its original state | The old town has been beautifully **preserved**. |
| restore | repair to its original condition | The temple was **restored** after the earthquake. |
| pass down / hand down | give to the next generation | The recipe was **passed down** from my grandmother. |
| revive | bring back into use | Young artists are **reviving** traditional weaving. |
| neglect | fail to look after | The fort was **neglected** for decades. |

### Famous people
| Word | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| renowned / acclaimed | famous and admired |
| influential | having a big effect on others |
| legacy | what a person leaves behind for the future |
| masterpiece | a person's best work of art |
| pioneer | one of the first people to do something |
| self-taught | learned without a teacher |

### Easily confused words
- **heritage** (culture of a group) vs **inheritance** (money/property you receive when someone dies) vs **heirloom** (a valuable object kept in a family for generations)
- **historic** (important in history: *a historic day*) vs **historical** (connected with the past: *historical documents*)

### With relative clauses
*Raden Sukma, **whose masterpiece** hangs in the national gallery, was a **self-taught** painter. Her **legacy**, **which** includes over 400 paintings, has been **preserved** by her family.*

> **Catatan:** *Heritage* = warisan budaya; *inheritance* = warisan harta; *heirloom* = pusaka keluarga. *Historic* = bersejarah (penting), *historical* = berkaitan dengan sejarah.

examples.en: Batik is an important part of Indonesia's cultural heritage.
examples.id: Batik adalah bagian penting dari warisan budaya Indonesia.

examples.en: The ancient temple, which had been neglected for years, was restored in 2015.
examples.id: Candi kuno itu, yang telah terbengkalai bertahun-tahun, dipugar pada 2015.

examples.en: This traditional dance has been passed down from generation to generation.
examples.id: Tari tradisional ini telah diwariskan dari generasi ke generasi.

examples.en: The renowned composer left a legacy that still inspires young musicians.
examples.id: Komponis terkenal itu meninggalkan warisan yang masih menginspirasi musisi muda.

vocabulary.example: The old quarter is a heritage site.

grammar.pattern: be passed down / handed down + from ... to ...
grammar.example: The ring was handed down from mother to daughter.

grammar.pattern: be renowned / famous / known + for + noun/-ing
grammar.example: The town is renowned for its silverwork.
The temple dates back to the 9th century.

mistakes.wrong: Batik is part of our cultural inheritance.
mistakes.right: Batik is part of our cultural heritage.
mistakes.why: Heritage is culture from the past; inheritance is money or property you receive.

mistakes.wrong: The town is renowned with its silverwork.
mistakes.right: The town is renowned for its silverwork.
mistakes.why: The preposition after renowned/famous is for.

mistakes.wrong: This is a historical day for our country.
mistakes.right: This is a historic day for our country.

sections.summary: Use **heritage, tradition, artefact, monument, indigenous, ancestor** for culture; **preserve, restore, pass down, revive, neglect** for protecting the past; and **renowned, influential, legacy, masterpiece, pioneer** for famous people. Don't confuse *heritage/inheritance/heirloom* or *historic/historical*. *Ringkasan: hati-hati dengan kata yang mirip.*

lessons.title: Writing Richer Descriptions
lessons.summary: Menulis deskripsi yang lebih kaya dengan which untuk seluruh klausa dan kuantitas + of whom/which.
objectives: Use which to comment on a whole clause
Use quantifier + of whom/which (most of whom, both of which)
Combine relative structures to write a fluent description
lessons.completionCriteria: Complete the writing task and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Selesaikan tugas menulis dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### 1. which referring to a whole clause
*Which* can comment on the **whole previous idea**, not just one noun. A comma is always needed.
- *The concert was cancelled, **which** disappointed everyone.* (= the cancellation disappointed everyone)
- *She speaks five languages, **which** is impressive.*

⚠️ Don't use *what* or *that* here: ✗ *..., what disappointed everyone.*

### 2. Quantifier + of + whom/which
Use this to give information about **part of a group**:
| Pattern | Example |
| --- | --- |
| all/most/many/some + of whom | *She has three brothers, **all of whom** are musicians.* |
| none/neither + of whom | *I invited ten friends, **none of whom** came.* |
| both/several/half + of which | *The village has two temples, **both of which** are 500 years old.* |
| the majority/a few + of which | *The museum received 200 letters, **most of which** were from children.* |

⚠️ Not *of them* after a comma: ✗ *three brothers, all of them are musicians* (this creates a comma splice; use *all of whom* or start a new sentence).

### 3. whose for things
*Whose* can also be used for things and places: *a town **whose** history goes back 1,000 years*.

### 4. Building a rich description
Compare:
- *Basic*: Raden Sukma was a painter. She was born in 1921. Her paintings are famous. She trained many students. Many of them now have studios.
- *Rich*: *Raden Sukma, **who was born in 1921**, was a self-taught painter **whose landscapes are now famous worldwide**. She trained dozens of young artists, **many of whom now run their own studios**, **which shows how influential she was**.*

### Tips for good descriptions
| Do | Avoid |
| --- | --- |
| mix short and long sentences | putting four relative clauses in one sentence |
| use reduced clauses (*built in 1820*) | repeating *which* again and again |
| use precise vocabulary (*renowned, legacy*) | vague words (*nice, good, very famous*) |

> **Catatan:** *, which* di akhir kalimat bisa merujuk ke **seluruh** klausa sebelumnya: *Konsernya dibatalkan, **dan hal itu** mengecewakan semua orang* → *The concert was cancelled, which disappointed everyone.* Untuk *sebagian besar dari mereka*, gunakan *most of whom* (orang) atau *most of which* (benda).

sections.summary: Use **, which** to comment on a whole clause, **quantifier + of whom/which** to describe part of a group, and **whose** for people, places and things. Combine these with reduced clauses and precise vocabulary for rich, fluent descriptions. *Ringkasan: most of whom (orang), most of which (benda).*
